Effortlessly simple: if you manage your long, complex, and secure passwords in a password manager app (like KeePassDroid) on your Android device, you can now “type” them easily, in public, without worrying about surveillance cameras or shoulder surfing, on any other device—phone, tablet, or PC—running Windows, Linux, or macOS.
sub rosa allows you to program the static password on your YubiKey, so you can “type” the password with the touch of a finger.
When you’re done “typing” your long, complex, and secure password, be sure to wipe your YubiKey clean.
It isn’t much security if someone else can “type” your password by touching the YubiKey.
sub rosa has support for OpenPGP. You can provision an OpenPGP key onto your YubiKey, Nitrokey 3, Nitrokey Pro or Librem Key.
In keeping with the app’s motto, “Effortlessly simple,” sub rosa allows you to encrypt, decrypt, sign, and authenticate with your security key, then wipe it clean and write another OpenPGP key to change your digital identity.
If you manage your OpenPGP keys with OpenKeychain or PGPony, importing OpenPGP keys in sub rosa is a breeze.

The source code is available at:
https://github.com/naive-HA/subrosa

By default, a YubiKey programmed with a static password will return the static password over NFC, without any guard, like a touch guards when connected over USB.
 Ideally, you would live by the sub rosa philosophy and program the static password, use it and then wipe it. But if you do not, then disabling the static password over NFC is your best alternative.

 Disabling the static password over NFC does not disable OpenPGP over NFC. Also, the static password over NFC can be re-enabled later on so that you can program the static password over NFC, not just over USB.

This sends only the first %1$d bytes of the firmware file (%2$d data reports of up to %3$d bytes) to the bootloader. That part holds the signed header of the file, which comes before any data that is written to the flash, so nothing is installed.\n\nThe bootloader then waits for the rest of the file. Afterwards unplug your Nitrokey 3 and plug it in again, and use REBOOT TO BOOTLOADER once more before you check or update.
